summary: Confirmed the extended experiment (receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064): after a client command returned success and was committed on the {A,B,E} leader, the healed cluster diverges — A's FSM holds six applied commands, the new leader's holds five — and the committed entry at the created index is truncated (both comparisons violated at witness 5). I then opened the complementary eligibility case as a child investigation: with C offline for its own removal, the restarted leader (flag on) lists the removed voter again (3 servers, 2 peers) while the serving peer reports 2, and when C returns, catches up and B is partitioned, one Apply on that leader returns success with A's commit index advancing to the entry while B — required by the configuration committed in the log — never receives it; with the flag off the identical sequence makes the leader refuse the write. That experiment is submitted with four comparisons (membership after restart, control, entry on a committed quorum, control refusal). The parent question now records all six receipts, the schedule-dependence of the leader-concurrency window, and the pending child receipt.
